group.passage:
Walk into an old church in Italy or a subway station in New York, and you may find a picture made of thousands of small pieces. This is a mosaic, an image built from bits of stone, glass, or tile pressed by hand into wet cement. Up close, each piece is only a [[1]] of color, but step back and the pieces join to form faces, animals, and entire landscapes. Because stone and glass do not fade the way paint does, mosaics are also remarkably [[2]].
The ancient Romans loved the art. Their grandest villas [[3]] floors covered with hunting scenes, sea creatures, and portraits of gods. The best of these works are so [[4]] that every feather of a bird and every wave of the sea can be seen. Many such floors have [[5]] earthquakes, floods, and wars, and archaeologists still uncover new ones around the Mediterranean today.
Mosaic reached new heights in the churches of the Byzantine Empire, where it climbed from the floor onto walls and ceilings. Artists backed small squares of glass with thin sheets of gold and placed each one at a slightly different [[6]], so that the walls seemed to glow in the light of candles. To the worshippers standing below, the effect must have been [[7]], as if heaven itself were shining down on them.
The art has never really disappeared. In the early twentieth century, Antoni Gaudí and his workers gave it a new [[8]] on life by covering the benches of a Barcelona park with broken tiles and plates. Today, mosaics brighten subway stations, swimming pools, and city walls around the world. The word itself has also [[9]] a wider meaning. A city where many cultures live side by side is often called a mosaic, a [[10]] made up of countless different parts that each keep their own color.

10.explanation_zh: whole 最常當形容詞「全部的、整個的」，這裡轉作名詞「整體」。a whole made up of countless different parts（由無數不同部分組成的整體）是 mosaic 的同位語，whole 和 parts 互相對照：各個文化保有自己的顏色，卻一起構成一座城市。

option_notes_zh.A: detailed（形容詞，細緻的、描繪入微的）不合：空格在 a 之後、made up of countless different parts 之前，需要單數名詞（和 mosaic 同位）。

option_notes_zh.E: durable（形容詞，耐久的、經久耐用的）不合：空格在 a 之後、made up of countless different parts 之前，需要單數名詞（和 mosaic 同位）。

option_notes_zh.I: angle（角度）不會由無數不同的部分組成，語意不通；angle 要放第 6 格。
option_notes_zh.J: dazzling（形容詞，耀眼奪目的）不合：空格在 a 之後、made up of countless different parts 之前，需要單數名詞（和 mosaic 同位）。

它由無數不同的「部分」組成，和 part 相對的概念是什麼？

translation_zh.text:
走進義大利的一座古老教堂，或紐約的一個地鐵站，你可能會看到一幅由成千上萬片小碎片組成的圖畫。這就是馬賽克：把石頭、玻璃或磁磚的小碎片用手壓進濕水泥裡拼成的圖像。近看時，每一小片只是一個色點，但退後一步，這些碎片就拼成了臉孔、動物和整片風景。因為石頭和玻璃不會像顏料那樣褪色，馬賽克也格外耐久。
古羅馬人熱愛這門藝術。他們最豪華的別墅擁有鋪滿狩獵場景、海洋生物和眾神肖像的地板。其中最好的作品細緻到連鳥的每一根羽毛、海的每一道波浪都看得清清楚楚。許多這樣的地板熬過了地震、洪水和戰爭，考古學家至今仍在地中海周圍不斷發現新的作品。
在拜占庭帝國的教堂裡，馬賽克達到新的高峰，從地板爬上了牆壁和天花板。工匠在小方塊玻璃背面貼上薄薄的金箔，並把每一塊擺成略微不同的角度，讓牆面在燭光中彷彿發出光芒。對站在下方的信徒來說，那效果想必耀眼奪目，彷彿天堂的光芒正照耀在他們身上。
這門藝術從未真正消失。二十世紀初，安東尼．高第（Antoni Gaudí）和他的工人用碎磁磚和破碗盤覆蓋巴塞隆納一座公園的長椅，讓馬賽克重獲新生。今天，馬賽克點亮了世界各地的地鐵站、游泳池和城市牆面。這個詞本身也有了更廣的意義。許多文化並存的城市常被稱為「馬賽克」：一個由無數不同部分組成、而每個部分都保有自己色彩的整體。

evidence: Up close, each piece is only a [[1]] of color, but step back and the pieces join to form faces, animals, and entire landscapes.

evidence: Because stone and glass do not fade the way paint does, mosaics are also remarkably [[2]].

evidence: Their grandest villas [[3]] floors covered with hunting scenes, sea creatures, and portraits of gods.
3.explanation_zh: boast 作及物動詞為「擁有（值得誇耀的東西）」，過去式 boasted。

evidence: The best of these works are so [[4]] that every feather of a bird and every wave of the sea can be seen.
4.explanation_zh: so detailed that 每根羽毛、每道浪都看得到，選 detailed。

evidence: Many such floors have [[5]] earthquakes, floods, and wars, and archaeologists still uncover new ones around the Mediterranean today.

evidence: To the worshippers standing below, the effect must have been [[7]], as if heaven itself were shining down on them.
7.explanation_zh: as if heaven itself were shining down 表示效果令人目眩，選 dazzling。

evidence: In the early twentieth century, Antoni Gaudí and his workers gave it a new [[8]] on life by covering the benches of a Barcelona park with broken tiles and plates.

evidence: The word itself has also [[9]] a wider meaning.

evidence: A city where many cultures live side by side is often called a mosaic, a [[10]] made up of countless different parts that each keep their own color.
